Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary assessment: Acute diarrhea for ~3 days with abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; 4–5 stools/day; stool described as watery/loose; no blood or mucus; able to maintain oral intake and fluids; not dehydrated on exam per clinician observation; asthma history; Lexapro use noted; family history of bowel cancer in father; no travel/exposure history reported.
- Differential diagnoses (top considerations aligned with transcript and DDx):
  - Acute viral gastroenteritis — High
  - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis — Medium
  - SSRI-induced diarrhea (Lexapro) — Medium
  - Inflammatory bowel disease flare — Low to Medium
- Note on DDx considerations: No conflicts between transcript and DDx identified; differential reasoning consistent with current presentation.

Management Plan
- Main plan: 
  - Continue oral hydration; consider oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) as needed
  - Diet: soft diet management during diarrhea; avoid dairy, fish, meat, eggs while diarrheal; progress to boiled vegetables and mash; if improved for 48 hours, reintroduce meat gradually
  - Probiotics: yoghurt recommended to help restore gut flora
  - If diarrhea persists or worsens: obtain stool sample if passing blood or if symptoms persist beyond one week
  - Monitor for dehydration: contact us if going 6–8 times/day or signs of dehydration develop; return for evaluation
  - Educate patient/app access: notes recorded in app for reference

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Acute viral gastroenteritis — High: Most consistent with acute diarrheal illness: onset ~3 days, 4–5 loose stools/day, watery stools, no blood, patient hydrated
- Acute bacterial gastroenteritis — Medium: Plausible given diarrhea and abdominal pain but less supported by absence of travel/exposure and fever
- SSRI-induced diarrhea (Lexapro) — Medium: Possible contribution from SSRI; temporal relationship not specified
- Inflammatory bowel disease — Low: Diarrhea with abdominal pain; absence of chronic history or hematochezia reduces likelihood
